facts.content: Patient has had 3 days of watery diarrhea approximately 6 to 7 times a day.
Patient experiences intermittent left lower quadrant crampy abdominal pain and feels weak and shaky.
facts.source_text: LLQ crampy abd pain; feels weak/shaky

facts.content: No blood is present in the stool.
Patient vomited at symptom onset, but it was non-bloody and has now resolved.
facts.source_text: Vomited at symptom onset (non-bloody); now resolved

facts.content: The patient had a subjective fever at onset 3 to 4 days ago but has no current fever.
facts.source_text: Subjective fever at onset (3–4 d ago); no current fever

facts.content: Appetite is decreased, but the patient is tolerating fluids and eating soups, smoothies, and light foods.
facts.source_text: Appetite ↓; tolerating fluids; eating soups/smoothies/light foods

facts.content: Possible trigger is Chinese takeaway 4 days ago; one sick contact with vomiting; no household diarrhea.
facts.source_text: Possible trigger: Chinese takeaway 4 d ago; sick contacts: one child vomited; no household diarrhea

facts.content: Patient needs proximity to a toilet and is still working as an accountant, although with difficulty.
facts.source_text: Impact: needs proximity to toilet; still working (accountant) but difficult

facts.content: Patient lives with wife and two children, is a non-smoker, and does not consume alcohol.
facts.source_text: SH: Lives w/ wife + 2 kids; non-smoker; no etOH

facts.content: The assessment is acute gastroenteritis with 3 days of watery diarrhea, left lower quadrant crampy intermittent pain, transient vomiting, and subjective fever at onset; tolerating fluids and no hematochezia. Probably viral but bacterial possible, with temporal association with takeaway 4 days ago.
facts.source_text: Acute gastroenteritis—3 d watery diarrhea, LLQ crampy intermittent pain; transient vomiting and subjective fever at onset; tolerating fluids; no hematochezia. Prob viral; bacterial possible. Temporal association w/ takeaway 4 d ago.

facts.content: Maintain hydration with oral rehydration salts such as Dioralyte.
facts.source_text: Conservative mgmt: maintain hydration; oral rehydration salts (e.g., Dioralyte)

facts.content: Provide symptomatic treatment with paracetamol, 2 tablets up to 4 times per day as needed.
facts.source_text: Symptomatic tx: paracetamol, 2 tablets up to 4x/day as needed

facts.content: Recommend rest and take 2 to 3 days off work.
If not improving in 3 to 4 days, review and consider stool studies.
facts.source_text: If not improving in 3–4 d: review; consider stool studies
